name: Make Square
description: We call an array $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_m$$$ good, if there exist two indices $$$i \lt j$$$ such that $$$b_i \cdot b_j$$$ is a perfect square . Given an array $$$b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_m$$$, in one action you can perform one of the following: multiply any element $$$b_i$$$ by any prime $$$p$$$; divide any element $$$b_i$$$ by prime $$$p$$$, if $$$b_i$$$ is divisible by $$$p$$$. Let $$$f(b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_m)$$$ be the minimum number of actions needed to make the array $$$b$$$ good. You are given an array of $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ and $$$q$$$ queries of the form $$$l_i, r_i$$$. For each query output $$$f(a_{l_i}, a_{l_i + 1}, \ldots, a_{r_i})$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$q$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 194\,598$$$, $$$1 \le q \le 1\,049\,658$$$) — the length of the array and the number of queries. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 5\,032\,107$$$) — the elements of the array. Each of the next $$$q$$$ lines contains two integers $$$l_i$$$ and $$$r_i$$$ ($$$1 \le l_i \lt r_i \le n$$$) — the parameters of a query.
output_specification: Output $$$q$$$ lines — the answers for each query in the order they are given in the input.
approach_summary: Precompute linear sieve to store minimum prime factor (spf[x]) up to N in O(N). Factorize any number x ≤ N in O(log x) steps.
